claim: for each predefined crash scenario, the signed audit proves the incident beyond doubt (chain + signatures verify, a tamper is caught) and the governing UK traffic law is inferred directly from the verified audit record + cited to the KB.

scenarios.name: civilian_runs_red
scenarios.description: A civilian car crosses the stop line against a red indication and collides.

governing_law.text: A driver who fails to comply with a lawfully-placed prescribed traffic sign (incl. traffic light signals) commits a criminal offence.
governing_law.why: the vehicle crossed the stop line against a red indication -- a criminal offence (RTA 1988 s36 / TS10)

governing_law.text: The red signal conveys the prohibition that vehicular traffic must not proceed beyond the stop line.
governing_law.why: the red signal conveys the prohibition that vehicular traffic must not proceed beyond the stop line

scenarios.name: ambulance_crosses_red_exempt
scenarios.description: An authorised, corroborated ambulance crosses red on an emergency run and conflicts with a car lawfully on green.

governing_law.text: An emergency vehicle may treat red as give-way and is NOT at fault merely for crossing red; fault arises ONLY on the para 5(5) endangerment test (it forced evasive action / endangered others).
governing_law.why: an authorised, corroborated emergency vehicle crossed red; not at fault merely for crossing (fault only on the endangerment test)

governing_law.text: Where a green-light driver collides with a red-crossing emergency vehicle, the default apportionment anchor is 60/40 against the non-emergency (green) driver.
governing_law.why: apportioning the EV-vs-other conflict: the default anchor is 60/40 against the non-emergency party

governing_law.text: Traffic proceeding beyond a stop line on green must proceed with due regard to the safety of other road users.
governing_law.why: the other party was on green but must proceed with due regard; typically the minority share (Joseph Eva)

scenarios.name: maintenance_runs_red
scenarios.description: A highway maintenance/works vehicle crosses red; it is NOT an emergency vehicle.

governing_law.text: Highway maintenance/works vehicles are NOT 'emergency vehicles' for the red-light exemption; a works vehicle crossing red is at fault exactly like an ordinary driver.
governing_law.why: a highway maintenance/works vehicle is NOT an emergency vehicle for the red-light exemption; crossing red it is at fault exactly like an ordinary driver

governing_law.text: A driver who fails to comply with a lawfully-placed prescribed traffic sign (incl. traffic light signals) commits a criminal offence.
governing_law.why: crossing the stop line against red is a criminal offence (TS10); near-conclusive of driver fault

scenarios.name: driver_crosses_on_amber
scenarios.description: A driver crosses on a steady amber when a safe stop was possible.

governing_law.text: A steady amber has the same effect as red; a driver who could have stopped safely but crossed is at fault. No fault only where too close to stop safely.
governing_law.why: the vehicle crossed on a steady amber when a safe stop was possible (same effect as red)

scenarios.name: conflicting_green_fault
scenarios.description: The signal system emits a conflicting green (a positively-wrong indication); two movements are released at once.

governing_law.text: An authority CAN be liable where it positively creates a trap (e.g. conflicting green signals) — misfeasance, not omission.
governing_law.why: the audit shows the system emitted a conflicting green (a positively-wrong indication) -- misfeasance, not omission

governing_law.text: A highway authority owes no private-law duty to provide/erect signs or warn (nonfeasance), and s.41 does not extend to signs/signals (Lord Hoffmann); liability only for misfeasance.
governing_law.why: authority fault otherwise defaults to zero; it turns non-zero only on this misfeasance/conflicting-green branch (low-confidence; legal_causation NOT_ASSESSED)

scenarios.name: dark_signal
scenarios.description: The signals are dark/inoperative at the time; a collision occurs at the junction.

governing_law.text: When traffic lights are not working (dark), the MUST duty to obey the signal falls away and each driver reverts to ordinary care as at an unmarked junction.
governing_law.why: the signal was dark/inoperative at the incident time, so the duty to obey it falls away (each driver reverts to ordinary care)

scenarios.name: spoofed_ev_triggers_red_run
scenarios.description: A compromised-but-approved neighbour signs a PHANTOM ambulance claim that commandeers the signal; a civilian then crosses the resulting red and collides. The audit attributes the triggering claim to the signing KEY.
